Can loss help a laser choose a wavelength?

A laser ring can support several wavelengths. Why would adding a second ring that absorbs light help one wavelength stand out?

In our invited review, we used a pair of coupled optical cavities to explain how gain and loss reshape the modes of a laser. Light can move between the two cavities. In the ideal balanced model, when gain and loss exceed the coupling strength, one mode grows while the other fades.

Experiments discussed in the review show how this can help select a wavelength. With suitable pumping and coupling, one mode can reach the lasing threshold while competing modes remain below it.

My students often ask what complex numbers are for. Here the imaginary part of a mode’s frequency tells us how quickly its field grows or fades.
